title: Two stacked keys at every length pair the old pre-filter dropped (plain, gap slack, mod 27-31, fixed multipliers, one clue letter out, word breaks counted), and autokey / progressive key numbered on A-Z or KRYPTOS, on 666,993 keyword tableaux
k4_result: 0 of 43,694,711,430 exact tests pass with 7 or more checks (666,993 alphabets x 65,510 tests; chance predicts about 0.5 passes in all, nearly all at exactly 7 checks). Nothing to decrypt. By part: stacked pairs on the 24 clue letters, all 41 pairs p<q<=13 plus 41 longer pairs (q 14-45): 0 of 546,934,260; gap off by 1-3: 0 of 820,401,390; mod 27-31: 0 of 666,993,000; fixed multipliers 3-23: 0 of 666,993,000; one clue letter left out: 0 of 4,148,696,460; word breaks counted: 0 of 32,362,500,360; autokey lags 1-6 with the fed letter numbered on A-Z or KRYPTOS: 0 of 320,156,640; progressive key moved on in another alphabet's order: 0 of 4,162,036,320. controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on A-Z, KRYPTOS and a different third of the alphabets (222,333 / 222,332 / 222,332, about 14.6 billion tests each): 0, 0, 0 pass with 7+ checks in every part (chance predicts about 0.17 each). Same picture as K4.
planted: 14/14 in a 16,676-alphabet sample (9 read as English, -4.28 to -4.68 with 0 wrong letters; 5 found by the exact test only because the clue letters fix too little key to read); idea-91 stacked map 41/41 pairs (82/82 textbook messages; attack 66 had 21/41); idea-91 attack-66 cells 437/438 found, 1 with too few checks to judge, 0 missed (attack 66 alone: 323/438, 115 missed)
scope_limits: Keyword tableaux from the repository's vocabulary only (plain keyword alphabets and the two transposition-mixed forms, 666,993 with A-Z and KRYPTOS), five layouts, Vigenere and Beaufort form. Stacked keys: two words only; of the pairs p<q<=13 the 13 with fewer than 7 checks stay undecidable from the clues: (7,12) (7,13) (8,11) (8,13) (9,10) (9,11) (9,13) (10,11) (10,12) (10,13) (11,12) (11,13) (12,13). The 41 longer pairs (second word 14-45 letters) were run on the plain 24 clue letters only. The variants (gap, modulus, multiplier, dropped letter, word breaks) were run only at the pairs the old filter dropped inside each variant's own stated scope (q<=13; gap +-1..3; N=27..31; multipliers 3..23; one letter out; 6 clue splits x 0-25 extra breaks), one variant at a time. Autokey: lags 1-6, one fixed lag, fed letter numbered on A-Z or KRYPTOS (numbering on M was attack 66), not combined with the variants and not the keyed-lag form of attack 74. Progressive: word length 1-12, constant step, moved on in A-Z, KRYPTOS or M order while looked up on a different cipher strip. Not rerun: attack 89 (non-keyword alphabets: QWERTY, Morse order, ...), which uses the same battery and so has the same two holes. No survivor appeared, so the reading stage ran on planted messages only; a survivor under 'word breaks', or at a pair whose graph is in pieces (second word 14, 21 or 42, some pairs after a dropped letter), could be read only in part.

negative.family: Key-rule battery holes: stacked key pairs and feed numbering
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a keyword tableau with two stacked repeating key words at one of the length pairs the round 9-11 pre-filter never let through, or an autokey / progressive key whose letters are numbered on A-Z or KRYPTOS instead of on the tableau's own keyword alphabet.
negative.scope: 666,993 keyword alphabets (dictionary keyword alphabets and both transposition-mixed forms, A-Z, KRYPTOS) x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort. Exact loop test (equal to the mod-13/mod-2 solve, no pre-filter), 7+ checks: two stacked keys at all 41 pairs p<q<=13 with 7+ checks, including the 20 dropped ones (3,11) (3,13) (4,11) (4,13) (5,9) (5,11) (5,12) (5,13) (6,9) (6,10) (6,11) (6,13) (7,8) (7,9) (7,10) (7,11) (8,9) (8,10) (8,12) (9,12), and at 41 longer pairs (q 14-45); the dropped pairs again with the gap between the clues off by 1-3 (123 tests per key stream), mod 27-31, fixed multipliers 3-23, each clue letter left out in turn (622), and word breaks using up key letters (4,852 over 156 position sets). Autokey at lags 1-6, plain and cipher feed, both signs, fed letter numbered on A-Z and on KRYPTOS (Quagmire I autokey with the key letter on the straight cipher strip, its mirror on the plain strip, rows picked by the carved A-Z labels). Progressive key of 1-12 letters moved on in A-Z, KRYPTOS or M order while looked up on a different strip, 26 index offsets. 43,694,711,430 exact tests.
negative.outcome: Dead: 0 tests pass with 7+ checks on K4 (chance predicts about 0.5); 3 shuffled K4s on a third of the alphabets each: 0, 0, 0; planted 14/14 in a 16,676-alphabet sample, idea-91 stacked map 41/41 (was 21/41), idea-91 attack-66 cells 437/438 with 0 missed (was 323/438 with 115 missed). The two holes the idea-91 audit found in attacks 66, 68, 70, 71B, 78, 81 and 88 are closed for these alphabets; the 13 pairs p<q<=13 with fewer than 7 checks stay undecidable, and attack 89's non-keyword alphabets were not rerun.

follow_ups: Rerun attack 89 (non-keyword alphabets: QWERTY, Morse order, historic alphabets) with kryptos.idea104_holes.test_alphabet: it calls kryptos.round11.battery, so it has the same two holes (20 dropped stacked pairs; autokey numbered only on the alphabet itself). A few minutes of CPU.

Fix kryptos.round11.battery and attacks/66 battery() in place: replace the 'c1 + c2 < min_checks + 1' pre-filter by kryptos.idea104_holes.Graph(pos, p, q).fits(k, n), which is exact for any modulus (the round11 version only has a necessary test for n != 26) and costs about one 4-term comparison per pair; then tests/test_idea_91.py can assert stacked_map 41/41 directly.

Two stacked keys where the second word is long (14-45 letters) gave 41 more decidable pairs on the plain clue letters; the same longer pairs were not run under gap slack, mod 27-31, a dropped clue letter or word breaks. Each variant has its own list of decidable long pairs (kryptos.idea104_holes.pairs(pos, 50)); running them is the same code with QMAX raised.
